section.title: Transactions
section.para: Code that changes several tables, and must not leave them half changed, can group the queries in a transaction: db_begin() starts it, db_commit() saves the changes and returns false if they were rolled back instead, and db_rollback() undoes them. Transactions can be nested: only the outermost db_commit() saves anything, and a db_rollback() at any level undoes the whole transaction.

MantisBT halts the request when a query fails, so there is no point in catching errors to roll back: a transaction that is still open at the end of the request is rolled back automatically. Work that cannot be rolled back, such as deleting files, should be done after db_commit(). Tables that do not support transactions (for example MyISAM ones) are not rolled back.
